data.title: U.S. Intelligence Says Iran Has Grown More Confident After Months of Fighting
data.description: According to Jin10, a new U.S. intelligence assessment says Iran has become more confident in its ability to strike U.S. military targets in the Middle East after more than six months of U.S. military action against it, and appears determined to keep confronting the United States at least until the November U.S. congressional midterm elections.

data.title: U.S. And China Plan Mid-September AI Safety Talks Led By Scott Bessent
data.description:
According to CNBC, the United States and China are preparing to hold official bilateral talks on AI safety risks in mid-September, with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent leading the U.S. side. The discussions would be the first bilateral meetings devoted exclusively to AI since President Donald Trump began his second term, and the agenda is expected to include cooperation on monitoring AI-directed cyberattacks, along with a U.S. proposal for American and Chinese AI labs to police themselves and share information to help prevent such attacks.

The talks come as Washington raises concerns about a future Chinese Mythos-level model with cyberattack capabilities and alleged Chinese distillation of proprietary U.S. AI models. On the Chinese side, the meeting could be led by Vice Premier He Lifeng, though Ding Xuexiang is also under consideration, while U.S. officials Michael Kratsios and Chinese science and technology minister Yin Hejun could attend. The final agenda, location and participants have not been set.

data.title: Leonardo CEO Mariani Sees Kyiv Unit as Deal Hub for Ukraine Defense Tech
data.description:
Leonardo SpA is using its new Kyiv unit to deepen ties with Ukraine’s fast-growing military-technology sector and is looking for partnership, investment or acquisition opportunities, Chief Executive Officer Lorenzo Mariani said, according to Bloomberg.

The Italian state-controlled defense company said the unit will serve as a base for those efforts.

data.title: Etihad CEO Says Airline Is Doubling Down on Growth Despite Iran War
data.description: According to CNBC, Etihad Airways entered 2026 after its most profitable year on record, but the Iran conflict disrupted flights, increased jet-fuel costs and pressured its rapid expansion. Group CEO Antonoaldo Neves said the airline is still adding planes and routes, is targeting break-even for the year and remains focused on growth after the conflict derailed its record-profit momentum.

data.title: Binance Wallet Expands LP Zap, Market Pages, and Web3 API Features
data.description: Binance announced on X that Binance Wallet has rolled out a weekly product update covering several areas across its wallet, web, and API tools. LP Zap now supports more EVM chains, while the LP position pop-up can display price ranges and remove liquidity. The market page has also been refreshed with an aggregated overview and dedicated Meme and stock sections. In addition, the tokenized stock detail page now includes access points for contract trading and the square feature. On the plugin side, a small-amount swap entry has been added, supporting conversions across up to 20 tokens. The update also includes new Web3 API functions for BSC-chain DeFi, B402 payments, and permission control. On the web interface, monitoring notification pop-ups now show market capitalization data to support trading decisions, search supports one-click purchases through Flash Buy, and token detail pages now allow custom indicator areas and a sidebar. The announcement did not provide further timing details for these features.

data.title: Listed Loan Facilitators Post Weaker Q2 Earnings as Delinquencies Improve
data.description:
Listed loan facilitation firms in China reported weaker second-quarter results, with revenue and net profit continuing to fall and JIayin Technology and Lufax posting losses, according to Jiemian News. JIayin Technology reported a net loss of 184 million yuan, while Qifu Technology, Xinye Technology, Lexin and Xiaoying Technology also posted sharply lower profit than a year earlier.

The downturn came after tighter funding supply and new rules from China's National Financial Regulatory Administration took effect on October 1, 2025, requiring related fees to be included in total financing costs and aligning business practices with a 24% annualized cap. Jiemian News reported that Lexin said a risk event involving some peers in late June tightened industry-wide funding supply and hurt market sentiment and loan volume.

Asset quality improved for some firms. Of seven listed loan facilitators that disclosed 90-day-plus delinquency rates, four saw the metric fall from the first quarter. As of June 30, 2026, delinquency rates were 2.1% for Xinye Technology, 9.09% for Xiaoying Technology, 2.83% for Qifu Technology and 2.21% for JIayin Technology, while Lexin, Lufax and Weijinsuo reported 3.6%, 3.7% and 8.64%, respectively.

Several companies struck a cautious tone for the third quarter. Xinye Technology CEO Li Tiezheng said the company would remain prudent in credit issuance rather than chase riskier volume. Qifu Technology said it expected third-quarter net profit and adjusted net profit to fall 67% to 73% year on year, while Lexin said total loan originations in the third quarter were likely to drop sharply from the second quarter and that it could post a net loss.

data.title: Listed Loan Facilitators Post Weaker Q2 Earnings as Delinquencies Improve
data.description:
Listed loan facilitation firms continued to see revenue and net profit decline in the second quarter of 2026, with Jiayin Group and Lexin both posting losses, according to Jiemian News. Jiayin Group reported a net loss of 184 million yuan, while Qifu Technology, Xinye Technology, Lexin and Xiaoying Technology all posted sharply lower profit than a year earlier.

The downturn came after China's National Financial Regulatory Administration issued a notice in April 2025 tightening oversight of internet loan facilitation by commercial banks, which took effect on October 1, 2025. The rule requires related fees such as credit enhancement charges to be included in the calculation of total financing costs, with business to be conducted under the judicial 24% annual cap. Jiemian News reported that tighter funding supply, stricter channel access and weaker loan origination weighed on earnings.

Asset quality improved for some firms. Of the seven listed loan facilitators that disclosed 90-day-plus delinquency rates, four reported lower ratios at the end of June than at the end of March. Xinye Technology, Xiaoying Technology, Qifu Technology and Jiayin Group reported 90-day-plus delinquency rates of 2.1%, 9.09%, 2.83% and 2.21%, down 1.01, 0.86, 0.67 and 0.04 percentage points from the first quarter, while Lexin, Lufax and WeCredit reported 3.6%, 3.7% and 8.64%, up 0.1, 0.3 and 0.53 percentage points.

Several companies struck a cautious tone for the third quarter. Xinye Technology CEO Li Tiezheng said the company would remain prudent in credit deployment rather than chase higher-risk volume. Qifu Technology said it expects third-quarter net profit and adjusted net profit to fall 67% to 73% year on year. Lexin said it expects total loan origination in the third quarter to drop sharply from the previous quarter and that it may post a net loss.

data.title: Bitcoin Drawdowns Have Narrowed Across Recent Cycles, Analysts Say
data.description:
Bitcoin market narratives have repeatedly centered on the idea that this time is different over the past 18 years, but the broader cycle structure has largely persisted. According to Odaily, BTC’s maximum drawdowns were about 85% in 2014, 84% in 2017, 77% in 2020 to 2021, and 53% in 2024 to 2025, showing a gradual decline in drawdown size.

Galaxy Digital head of firmwide research Alex Thorn shared a chart saying the current BTC drawdown is noticeably smaller than in earlier cycles. Analyst Willy Woo said Bitcoin may be shifting from a four-year cycle to a six-year to eight-year cycle as the supply shock from halvings weakens, though he said the view cannot yet be confirmed.

Previous cycles saw gains from the bottom to the next all-time high of about 580 times, 130 times, 22 times, and 8 times. Analyst James Check said Bitcoin’s cycle lows have moved higher each round while tops have remained relatively stable, and Jesse Myers said BTC may have just entered a two-year to three-year bull market.
